rationale: Diff is oversized (255KB), so this round's coverage of the ~59 touched endpoints rests on lens output plus targeted spot checks, not an exhaustive read. Standards audit found 2 blocking issues (commit-format colon, Optional vs str | None in a new module) at partial status. 4 additional real defects verified against source: metrics_elastic_repository.py's ES exception handling misses generic TransportError/asyncio.TimeoutError; main.py's model-provider readiness check runs boto3 credential resolution synchronously inside async lifespan with no deadline; analytics.py's leaderboard trigger endpoint checks auth before the feature-flag guard while every read endpoint checks the flag first; and job_lock.py/main.py/toolkit_service.py/tools_info_service.py/provider_service.py/tool_execution_service.py gate on retrieval_available() alone (RETRIEVAL_BACKEND != none) instead of ElasticSearchClient.is_configured() (which also checks ELASTIC_URL), so they still construct an ES client when RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=elasticsearch but ELASTIC_URL is unset. 1 deferred: FEATURE_CLI_ANALYTICS/customer-config.yaml migration mismatch is out of this task's explicit scope. 9 dismissed as noise: AnalyticsService's fail_open_on_unavailable=True default was verified correct by design (repository default is False; only AnalyticsService's own construction opts in, Leaderboard/StaleDatasource stay fail-closed); ADMIN_LOG_LOOKUP_ENABLED default True is already admin-gated; nginx /healthcheck hardcoded 200 has no established external caller (Docker HEALTHCHECK correctly hits the proxied endpoint); entrypoint.sh's PID-kill race is low-impact given the 60s poll already catches a crashed uvicorn; the bare except around AWS credential resolution is explicitly documented as an intentional startup-resilience tradeoff; _LEADERBOARD_COMPONENT_ID was verified to match the actual YAML id (no mismatch); MetricsElasticRepository's logger.exception() call outside an except block is a cosmetic logging defect only; the RETRIEVAL_BACKEND downgrade/stale-IndexInfo scenario is already documented as an accepted limitation in job_lock.py; and _bedrock_session()'s uncaught construction path is already absorbed by main.py's outer except Exception, only losing message detail.

standards_review.notes: guide requires EPMCDME-####: Description; 21 of 22 subjects in range match, but 'EPMCDME-14653 Model Provider startup handling' omits the colon separator required by README.md:163

guide requires new modules to use X | None over typing.Optional; new file model_provider_readiness.py imports Optional and declares 'provider: Optional[str]' instead of 'str | None'; other changed files only retain pre-existing Optional usage
fallback logic logs only exception text/reason strings, never credentials; model_provider_readiness.py logs setting names not values; .env.standalone.example uses placeholders only

findings.file: commit subject: 'EPMCDME-14653 Model Provider startup handling'
findings.title: Commit subject omits required colon
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires the format 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; this subject omits the colon separator.
findings.impact: Breaks the documented ticket-prefixed commit convention the squash-merge policy relies on.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'EPMCDME-14653: Model Provider startup handling' (only relevant if this commit is rewritten before merge).

findings.title: ES exception handling misses generic transport errors
findings.problem: All three graceful-degradation except clauses (lines ~128, ~192, ~253) catch only (elasticsearch.ConnectionError, ConnectionTimeout). elastic_transport's TlsError is a ConnectionError subclass so it is already covered, but the base TransportError, SerializationError, SniffingError, and asyncio.TimeoutError are siblings, not subclasses, and are not caught.
findings.impact: A real ES outage that surfaces as one of the uncaught transport-level exception types still propagates as an unhandled 500 instead of the intended graceful 200-empty/503 degradation, only partially delivering the stated goal.
findings.recommendation: Broaden the except clause to catch elastic_transport.TransportError (which covers ConnectionError, ConnectionTimeout, SerializationError, SniffingError) alongside asyncio.TimeoutError.

findings.title: Model-provider readiness check blocks async lifespan
findings.problem: _check_model_provider_readiness(app) is called directly (not via asyncio.to_thread) from the async lifespan(). It calls the synchronous check_model_provider_readiness(), which calls boto3.Session.get_credentials() synchronously. The module's own docstring states the credential chain as a whole has no overall deadline: a credential_process provider 'runs an external command that botocore does not time out at all'.
findings.impact: A misconfigured AWS credential_process can hang the event loop during startup indefinitely, contradicting the code's own stated goal that this check 'never blocks startup'.
findings.recommendation: Run check_model_provider_readiness() via asyncio.to_thread() (as already done elsewhere in main.py's lifespan, e.g. recover_orphaned_workflow_states) so a hanging credential_process cannot block the event loop.

findings.title: Leaderboard endpoints order authz/feature-flag checks inconsistently
findings.problem: Every leaderboard read endpoint (lines 3433-3713) lists Depends(_require_leaderboard_enabled) before Depends(admin_or_maintainer_or_auditor_access), so the 503 feature-flag check runs before authentication/authorization. trigger_leaderboard_computation (line 3683) does the opposite: Depends(admin_access_only) before Depends(_require_leaderboard_enabled).
findings.impact: An unauthenticated/unauthorized caller can learn whether LEADERBOARD_ENABLED is on from the read endpoints (503 vs proceeding to the auth check) while the trigger endpoint does not leak this, an inconsistent, minor information-disclosure pattern across the same feature.
findings.recommendation: Put Depends(_require_leaderboard_enabled) consistently after the access-control dependency on every leaderboard route (matching trigger_leaderboard_computation), or vice versa, but pick one order and apply it uniformly.

findings.title: New module uses typing.Optional instead of str | None
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires 'X | None' unions in new modules instead of typing.Optional; this new file imports 'from typing import NamedTuple, Optional' and declares 'provider: Optional[str]' in ModelProviderReadiness.
findings.impact: Documented blocking code-quality standard for new modules is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'Optional[str]' with 'str | None' and drop the Optional import (add 'from __future__ import annotations' if needed for NamedTuple field evaluation).

findings.title: ES-availability guards use retrieval_available() instead of is_configured()
findings.problem: retrieval_available(config) only checks RETRIEVAL_BACKEND != 'none'; it does not check whether ELASTIC_URL is actually set. ElasticSearchClient.is_configured() correctly combines both checks, but job_lock.py:120, main.py:797/990/998, provider_service.py:80, tool_execution_service.py:312, tools_info_service.py:77/80, and toolkit_service.py:1179 all call retrieval_available(config) directly instead of is_configured().
findings.impact: When RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=elasticsearch (the default) but ELASTIC_URL is blank/unset, these call sites believe retrieval is available and proceed to build/use an ES client that is not actually configured, contradicting the requirement to never construct the ES client when the capability says unavailable, and failing hard instead of degrading gracefully.
findings.recommendation: Gate these call sites on ElasticSearchClient.is_configured() instead of retrieval_available(config) directly, or fold the ELASTIC_URL check into retrieval_available() itself.
